nodes.question: Is the requested mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: pass: The requested mug is identifiable and visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The requested mug is identifiable and visibly not to their right. unknown: Target correspondence or its final relative position cannot be established. Describe the relevant mug, headphones, and their locations; merely finding some mug-like object on the right is insufficient when multiple candidates make correspondence ambiguous.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited endpoint independently of any progress observation. Use the source image to identify the requested mug: the single light-blue mug with a curved handle left of the black headphones. Use visible shape, handle, appearance, and scene correspondence together; exact color or pixel preservation is not an additional requirement. Do not assume that an added-looking mug is a duplicate or that a blurred region is the original mug. Source comparison identifies the target, but proving a movement trajectory is unnecessary for a known endpoint.

nodes.question: What image-grounded evidence, if any, establishes progress on relocating the requested mug to the headphones' right?
nodes.criteria: pass: Visible evidence establishes some requested relocation progress; describe the concrete change and whether it establishes an incomplete or completed result. fail: The images establish no requested relocation progress, such as the identifiable target remaining unchanged while only unrelated objects or scene details change. unknown: The evidence cannot distinguish requested progress from unrelated changes or ambiguous object correspondence. Neither a change of any kind nor a right-side unidentified mug alone establishes progress. Do not require a reconstructed editing operation or a particular trajectory.
nodes.binding: Compare source and edited images directly, tracking the requested source mug using multiple visible features and scene correspondence. Assess progress toward the requested relative placement rather than arbitrary displacement. Distinguish evidence of relocation from uncertain disappearance, added objects, and appearance changes; these possibilities are hypotheses, not predetermined findings. Inspect independently even if endpoint correspondence is unresolved, and report any independently grounded progress evidence without inventing continuity.

nodes.question: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric using the supports' grounded evidence, not confidence or pass counts. Return complete when s1 establishes that the requested mug is to the right of the headphones; s2 unknown or skipped must not block this endpoint. Equivalent grounded endpoint evidence in s2 may also establish completion. Otherwise return partial when evidence establishes some requested progress without establishing complete fulfillment, including when endpoint uncertainty coexists with independently established progress. Return absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress; s1 fail alone does not establish absence. Return unknown when neither completion, requested progress, nor absence of progress is established. Unknown and skipped states are not failures. Ambiguous target identity must not be resolved by selecting an arbitrary right-side mug, and unrelated additions or alterations do not count as progress. If support evidence conflicts about target correspondence or placement, preserve uncertainty unless the evidence itself resolves the conflict.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.
